headerDesc: Hit distribution of the 13 REL rules across all analyzed papers, with human-judged precision.
orphanWarning: {count} judgments belong to papers that have been deleted — they still count toward overall / per-rule, but cannot be broken down by severity / confidence (their result_json is gone).
severityHint: Ideal: higher severity should mean higher precision — i.e. the LLM doesn't flag minor issues as high severity.
confidenceHint: Ideal: precision for the high-confidence range > mid > low. Without this trend the confidence signal is broken and the prompt needs reworking.
colTotalDefectsTitle: How many defects this rule caught in total
colFiredPapersTitle: Number of papers that triggered this rule
colJudgedTitle: Number of defects judged by the reviewer
fireRateExplain: : papers fired / papers analyzed. Too low (≤10%) may mean the rule is too strict or the Cypher is incomplete; too high (≥80%) may be over-firing.
precisionExplain: : (correct + 0.5 × partial) / judged count. < 0.5 means the rule description or Cypher should be rewritten.
statusGoodDesc: ≥ 3 judged and precision ≥ 70% — stable rule with a low false-positive rate.
statusReviewDesc: ≥ 3 judged but precision < 50% — high false-positive rate; consider rewriting the rule description or Cypher.
statusHighFireDesc: Hit rate > 80% — fires on almost every paper, possibly over-firing; review the rule or Cypher.
statusNeverFireDesc: Total defects = 0 — the rule is too strict or the Cypher matched no candidates; needs a sample paper to verify.
statusWorkingDesc: The rule fires but there aren't enough judgments (< 3) — quality can't be assessed yet; needs more reviewer labels.
statusNoDataDesc: The system hasn't analyzed any papers yet; no rule has run.
neverFireTitle: Never fired. The rule may be too strict or the Cypher matched no candidates.
reviewTitle: Precision below 50%; consider rewriting the rule description.
highFireTitle: Fires on almost every paper, possibly over-firing.
rulesSubtitle: Converged from 51 section-level rules via MECE

ruleDesc.REL-01: Every claim should be backed by corresponding evidence — quantitative data, citations, experimental results, or logical reasoning.
ruleDesc.REL-02: When a baseline is mentioned in Method/Experiment, its limitations or shortcomings should be critiqued.
ruleDesc.REL-03: Every key research decision (choosing a dataset / metric / architecture) should be justified.
ruleDesc.REL-04: The paper should have a clear macro-level decomposition — the big problem split into sub-problems, and sub-problems into sub-methods.
ruleDesc.REL-05: Steps in the Method section should follow a clear order (what comes first, then next), expressed with proper connectives or numbering.
ruleDesc.REL-06: Newly introduced concepts/terms/variables should be formally defined (mathematical or operational definition, or a formula) — not just analogies or vague descriptions.
ruleDesc.REL-07: The Experiment section should specify the experimental setup scope (data, hyperparameters, hardware, evaluation protocol).
ruleDesc.REL-08: The paper should have a clear "problem → solution" mapping — every problem raised in the Introduction should have a corresponding solution.
ruleDesc.REL-09: In the Results / Discussion / Experiment sections, noteworthy observations should be attributed or explained.
ruleDesc.REL-10: After acknowledging a limitation (concession) there should be a compensation strategy — e.g. future work, a viable alternative, or a scope clarification.
ruleDesc.REL-11: Specific cases should lead to a generalization, and conversely a generalization should be supported by specific cases.
ruleDesc.REL-12: The Conclusion should restate the paper's core claims (consistent with the core of the Abstract/Introduction).
ruleDesc.REL-13: The paper should include appropriate meta-discourse (e.g. "this section introduces…", "the next section discusses…", section guidance).
